Skip to main content

This exercise is part of an accessibility laboratory. The same reporting journey is rebuilt in different rendering models so the failures can be compared and tested.

  • Laboratory catalogue
  • Report a hedgehog (React)
  • Report a wombat (Vue)
  • Report a paca (Web Components)

'Record a goose sighting' accessibility exercise instructions

'Record a goose sighting' is a made-up government service, filled with accessibility issues. Your task is to find them all!

To help find the issues, install Accessibility Insights for Web in Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome. Start with Fast Pass, then use Tab stops and the manual checks to find what automated checks cannot. You'll also need to try to complete the exercise using just your keyboard. Read the tips on what to look for and how to record your findings.

There are 6 pages in total:

  • Start page
  • Do you like geese?
  • What type of goose did you see?
  • When did you see the goose?
  • Check your answers
  • Confirmation page

Accessibility issues start on the next page. Good luck!

Continue

Want more keyboard practice? Try the focus practice page, which contains failures that Fast Pass does not report.

If you'd like to know more about the background, visit the blog post about this, 'Training people to do accessibility reviews'.

If you'd like to go straight to the answers, view the answers page - no cheating though!

Known limitations

  • Routine commit detail is retained for 30 days; pull requests, issues, reviews, and releases are retained for the full lookback window.
